title: Mental Math
subtitle: 30 sums, each harder, each with a trick

cards.note: Think of the sequence 5, 6, 7, 8: 56 = 7 × 8.
Round up: 45 + 40 = 85, then take away 2. Your head is far more reliable with round numbers.
Count up from 37: 3 to reach 40, then 60 to reach 100, together 63. That is how cashiers count out change.
10 percent means moving the decimal point one place left. Everything else builds on it: 5% is half of that, 20% double.
Times 5 means times 10, then halve: 480 ÷ 2 = 240.
Split the number: 10 × 6 = 60 and 7 × 6 = 42, together 102.
12 × 12 = 144, known as a gross. Knowing the squares up to 20² by heart saves time constantly.
25 is a quarter of 100: 16 ÷ 4 = 4, so 400. Times 25 always means divide by 4 and multiply by 100.
10% is 8, and 5% is half of that, so 4. Together 12, the classic tipping trick.
Halve three times: 180, 90, 45. Dividing by 8 is just dividing by 2 three times.
18 plus half of 18: 18 + 9 = 27. Times 1.5 always means the number plus its half.
10% is 4.5, double that is 9. Alternatively: 20% is a fifth, and 45 ÷ 5 = 9.
Look for partners that make round numbers: 47 + 53 = 100, plus 36 makes 136. Order does not matter when adding.
The 11 trick: spread the digits apart and put their sum in the middle. 4, then 4 + 3 = 7, then 3 gives 473.
Work out 100 × 7 = 700 and subtract 7 once. Times 99 is always times 100 minus the number once.
Take each digit to 9 and the last one to 10: 3, 4, 7 become 6, 5, 3. This works for any subtraction from a power of ten.
A quarter is 30, three quarters are 90. Divide by the bottom number first, then multiply by the top.
Times 0.5 is the same as halving: half of 0.4 is 0.2. Or 5 × 4 = 20, then place two decimal digits.
Dividing by a half means doubling. Mixing it up with halving gets you 36.
Percentages can be swapped: 8% of 25 is the same as 25% of 8, which is a quarter of 8.
23 × 20 = 460, then add one more 23: 483. Numbers just above a round number are best split like this.
To square a number ending in 5, multiply the front digit by the next number up, 2 × 3 = 6, then append 25. That gives 625.
12.5% is one eighth. These fractions pay off: 25% is a quarter, 12.5% an eighth, 20% a fifth.
125 is one eighth of 1000. So times 125 means times 1000, divided by 8.
196 lies between 13² = 169 and 15² = 225. A square ending in 6 has a root ending in 4 or 6, so 14.
(20 − 1)² = 400 − 40 + 1 = 361. Just below a round number, the binomial formula pays off.
Remember 2¹⁰ ≈ 1000. Then 2²⁰ is roughly a million, handy for memory sizes and probabilities.
(100 − 2)(100 + 2) = 100² − 2² = 10000 − 4. The difference of squares turns pairs like this into one line.
Same trick as for 25²: 8 × 9 = 72, then append 25. It works for every number ending in 5.
